s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive weight loss with a palpable abdominal mass and anemia
salient_findings: Palpable mass in the right iliac fossa
Drop in hemoglobin from 13 g/dL to 10 g/dL
key_facts: 52-year-old woman with well-controlled HIV
Viral load <40 copies/mL
CD4 count 290 cells/mm3
20% weight loss (12 kg) over one year
Initial weight loss was intentional but accelerated in recent months
No fevers, night sweats, gastrointestinal symptoms, or gynecological complaints
Palpable mass in the right iliac fossa
Drop in hemoglobin from 13 g/dL to 10 g/dL
Lactate dehydrogenase level of 643 U/L
C-reactive protein level of 80 mg/L
Normal white-cell count
History of hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002
CT scan showed a 15 cm mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall
Potential fistulous connection to the cecum
Mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm
No distant metastases
Serum tumor markers (CA19-9, CEA, CA125) were all negative

shortlist.label: Vaginal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall with a potential fistulous connection to the cecum

shortlist.label: Cervical cancer recurrence
shortlist.why_kept: History of hysterectomy for micro-invasive cervical carcinoma and presence of a large pelvic mass

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Palpable mass in the right iliac fossa and weight loss, although no gastrointestinal symptoms

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Anemia, elevated lactate dehydrogenase, and mesenteric lymph nodes measuring up to 27 mm

shortlist.label: Ovarian cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Large pelvic mass and anemia, although serum tumor markers were negative

raw.rationale: History of micro-invasive cervical carcinoma in 2002 and presence of a large mass possibly arising from the vaginal wall with a potential fistulous connection to the cecum, suggesting local recurrence and spread.

rejected.label: Vaginal cancer
rejected.why: While possible, the history of cervical cancer and the location of the mass suggest recurrence is more likely than a new primary vaginal cancer.

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer
rejected.why: The mass's potential connection to the cecum could suggest this, but the patient's history and the mass's origin from the vaginal wall make cervical cancer recurrence more plausible.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: Normal white-cell count and lack of systemic symptoms like fevers or night sweats make lymphoma less likely.

rejected.label: Ovarian cancer
rejected.why: The mass's described origin from the vaginal wall and the patient's history of cervical cancer make ovarian cancer a less likely explanation for the findings.
